cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet has a word from the LORD, and it's for one man: Baruch son of Neriah, who's been getting Jeremiah's words down. A personal word from the LORD, friend, for ONE guy. The most personal message I ever got was a price sticker that said 25 CENTS.

cards.question: When this word comes, Baruch is writing Jeremiah's words down on a ___.

cards.text: Jeremiah talks and Baruch writes, word for word, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah. Baruch is basically Jeremiah's voice-to-text, except voice-to-text never gets a HAND CRAMP.

cards.question: The LORD speaks to Baruch by name and starts with Baruch's own words. How has Baruch been feeling?
Baruch says the LORD has added sorrow on top of the pain he already had.

cards.text: Baruch's complaint gets an ANSWER, friend, which is more than my groaning ever got from the back of a junk drawer. Jeremiah passes along the LORD's answer, and it starts with the whole land.

cards.question: Throughout the land, the LORD says He will demolish and uproot. Whose work is coming down?

answers.text: What He Himself built and planted
What the kings of Judah built and planted

cards.text: Then the LORD turns from the whole land right back to Baruch, with a question about what Baruch has been reaching for. Friend, I know reaching: I once stretched my mustache for the top shelf and brought the WHOLE cookie jar down on my hat.

cards.question: The LORD asks Baruch about what he's reaching for. What does He ask if Baruch is seeking?
The LORD tells Baruch to keep reaching for great things for himself.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD tells him, "Stop seeking!" I need that taped above my ovens, friend, because some mornings I'm out here trying to stamp the FANCIEST cookie in the whole Dorinverse.

cards.question: Next the LORD says He will bring disaster. What will it fall on?
But wherever Baruch goes, the LORD will grant him his ___ as a spoil of war.

findings.problem: The card twice describes this as a word from the LORD. Verse 1 supplies Jeremiah, Baruch and the writing setting, but the LORD addressing Baruch is explicit in verse 2. The story card's citation is therefore too narrow and should include verse 2.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 1 says only that Baruch has been getting Jeremiah's words down. It gives no basis for reasoning that he wrote on a scroll rather than a wall or tablet, so this blank tests an unseen detail by luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card explicitly tells the transition from the LORD's message about the whole land in verse 4 back to Baruch in verse 5, but it cites only verse 5. Under the exact-citation rule, its range should include both verses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Six of the eight choice cards—2, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 12—ask for details that earlier cards neither supply nor make inferable: the writing material, Baruch's condition, the sorrow added to his pain, whose work is demolished, what Baruch is seeking and what the disaster strikes. Discovery questions consequently dominate the stop instead of remaining a few exceptions among mostly informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
